title: Technology Sector Update for 07/13/2018: AAPL,GOGO,PIXY,BRKR

Technology stocks were narrowly lower Friday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing nearly 0.2% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a 0.3% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Apple ( AAPL ) was slightly higher Friday, topping out with a 0.4% rise, after the technology giant disclosed plans to launch a clean energy fund in China that will connect suppliers with renewable energy sources as part of efforts to address climate change. The company said the $300 million China Clean Energy Fund will invest in and develop renewable energy and alternative fuels projects totaling more than 1 gigawatt of renewable energy in China, the equivalent of powering nearly 1 million homes. The fund also looks to provide participants with the advantage of greater purchasing power and realizing more attractive and diverse clean energy solutions.
In other sector news:
+ Gogo ( GOGO ) retreated Friday, sinking as much as 18%, despite the in-flight connectivity company reiterating its FY18 revenue guidance, saying it is set to reach free cash flow break-even by 2020 as well as generate significant yearly EBITDA growth, which is seen rising to more than $200 million in 2022. CEO Oakleigh Thorne said the recent initiatives are positioning Gogo for sustainable value creation, adding he expects to reduce cash burn at the company by over $100 million in FY19 from prior-year levels and by a further $100 million in 2020. The firm maintained its revenue target of $865 million to $935 million for 2018, in line with its prior guidance and market expectations for $885.96 million in revenue this year.
+ ShiftPixy ( PIXY ) soared over 90% higher on Friday after the staffing software firm issued preliminary fiscal Q3 financial results, projecting a net loss of $0.06 per share for the three months ended May 31, improving on a $0.11 per share net loss during the year-earlier period, as revenue more than doubled year-over-year, rising to $9.4 million from $4.6 million last year. The workforce platform company also said gross billings more than doubled over last year to $60.2 million, compared to $27.5 million for the March-to-May reporting period in 2017. The company said it expects to provide a new release date for its Q3 results as soon as possible.
- Bruker ( BRKR ) fell almost 2% on Friday after the scientific instruments and measurements company late Thursday said it acquired JPK Instruments AG, a biomolecular and cellular imaging company based in Berlin, Germany. The target company also provides force measurements on single molecules, cells and tissues. It generated around EUR10 million, or about $11.7 million, in annual revenue during 2017. Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
